analysis: Pseudotumour cerebri, also known as idiopathic intracranial hypertension, is a condition characterized by increased intracranial pressure without an identifiable cause. Among the options provided, Tetracycline is known to be associated with increased intracranial pressure and has been documented in medical literature as a potential cause of Pseudotumour cerebri. The other drugs listed (Sparfloxacin, Gentamicin, and Clofazimine) do not have a well-established link to this condition. Therefore, based on the known pharmacological effects and documented cases, Tetracycline is the most likely drug to cause Pseudotumour cerebri. The reasoning chains support this conclusion, indicating a strong association with Tetracycline and a lack of association with the other options. Thus, the best-supported option is Tetracycline.
